title: Collect widely, write about the best
statement: Have learners collect more evidence than they will use and write about only the strongest of it.
example: In one Grade 3 design the learner finds three quotations and writes about the best two.
detail: A Grade 9 unit carries in a decision from an earlier unit: students collect a range of evidence but write about only the best of it, with no fixed number of quotes. A review of the unit's prototype found a counter in independent practice that conflicts with the decision if all three quotes it counts must be analysed, and left that open. A Grade 3 lesson design makes choosing the best evidence its own step once three clues are collected.
against: The two designs differ on fixing the numbers: the Grade 3 design fixes three found and two picked, with an "n of 3 found" tracker (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 71 and 248), while the Grade 9 decision sets no fixed number. Whether the Grade 9 prototype's "1 of 3" counter means collection or three required analyses is open (`g9/sources/Othello_1_Feedback_DevFactory.md`, line 126).

evidence.quote: Students collect a range of evidence but write about only the best of it. No fixed number of quotes.
Three mandated break-downs is a fixed number. If the three are collection this is fine; if all three must be analyzed, it contradicts the decision.
